Docker docs: "A Docker image digest is a unique, cryptographic identifier (SHA-256 hash) representing the content of a Docker image." A hash of content carries no pusher identity; second half follows from this.

Sigstore Cosign signing overview, in order: "An in-memory public/private keypair is created." then "The identity token is retrieved."; "Fulcio issues short-lived certificates binding an ephemeral key to an OpenID Connect identity."; "the private key is destroyed shortly after and the short-lived identity certificate expires." Sigstore runs Fulcio (CA) and Rekor (log): "Signing events are logged in Rekor". Diagram now shows key pair first and signing after the certificate, matching this order.

GitHub OIDC reference: "The job or workflow must grant the `id-token: write` permission to allow GitHub's OIDC provider to create a JSON Web Token"; "Without `id-token: write`, the OIDC JWT ID token cannot be requested."

GitHub OIDC docs example token: `"iss": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"`, `"repository": "octo-org/octo-repo"`, `"ref": "refs/heads/main"`, `"job_workflow_ref": "octo-org/.../.github/workflows/oidc.yml@refs/heads/main"`; header `"alg": "RS256"`. Signed: Fulcio issuing overview "Download the issuer's signing keys from the discovery endpoint", "Verify the ID token signature".

Fulcio issuing overview: "Use the issuer claim from the token to find the issuer's OIDC discovery endpoint", "Download the issuer's signing keys", "Verify the ID token signature". CA overview: "Fulcio signs X.509 certificates valid for 10 minutes."

OIDC in Fulcio: certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"; certificate-identity "https://github.com/USERNAME/REPOSITORY_NAME/.github/workflows/WORKFLOW_NAME@refs/heads/BRANCH_NAME"; job_workflow_ref "is included as a SAN URI: https://github.com/{job_workflow_ref}". release.yml:11-13 only `contents: write`, `packages: write`; no `id-token`, no `cosign` anywhere in the file. :50-61 step "Check that each version tag names the signed digest": `[ "$signed" = "$released" ] || { echo "::error::...is not the digest CI signed"; exit 1; }`. stage-3..HEAD diff touches only release.yml's checkout pin (@@ -16,7 +16,7 @@).

Sigstore security model: "Fulcio assumes that a valid OIDC token from a trusted provider is sufficient"; "The identity and issuer associated with the OIDC token is embedded in the short-lived certificate". GitHub's issuer is a configured Fulcio issuer and any job granted id-token: write gets a token. cosign_verify.md: identity or identity-regexp "must be set for keyless flows".

Fulcio puts job_workflow_ref in the SAN: "https://github.com/{job_workflow_ref}" (oidc-in-fulcio). release.yml runs `on: push: tags: ['v*.*.*']`, so its SAN would be .../.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v…, not verify-image.sh:19 `.../ci.yml@refs/heads/master`.

Signing overview: "For security, the private key is destroyed shortly after and the short-lived identity certificate expires." No key is kept, so none to rotate or back up; trust at verification rests on --certificate-identity/--certificate-oidc-issuer (cosign_verify.md).

But `--tlog-upload` is not in that page's Options list, so "defaults to true" as a flag default was not seen. Lesson §3 wording ("by default") is supported. claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Cosign 3.1 uploads keyless signatures to the public transparency log unless told not to (its sign reference shows `--tlog-upload=false` to skip it); the log only grows and is public, so anyone can read the entries made for an identity.

Nobody in the lesson ever looks at the log for an identity, so I do not see why that purpose matters here.
